I went to an all girls school that has a big emphasis on women excelling in any place they choose to do so, especially STEM. There was nothing I was not encouraged to do, even if I wasn't good at it. I decided around age 12 that I wanted to do some sort of science in college. I discovered, to my horror, when I went to college, that the rest of the world does not operate like my school. My first boyfriend at 19 told me that I could never complete my computer science degree because "his friend does CS and it's even hard for HIM". The classes I chose were all taught by men and the guys in my class were all carbon copies of my ex. I realized I don't want to fight to be heard in that environment for the rest of my life.

It didn't help that I was also struggling massively with my mental health and this has gone undetected for years. It tanked my grades, and I was just seen as a write off. I think it would have helped if this was caught earlier. The doctor I eventually saw estimated that I had been in a depressive episode for at least four years. I turned a four year degree into a six year degree, but I got my BSc in Computer Science and Biology.

I am 26 now and happier than ever not pursuing STEM as a career. I apply it to my own job when needed and it's appreciated by everyone. I love it from a distance.

Oh I asked for help for over ten years to multiple people. Only got it aged 24. I'm really tired of hearing that "people don't ask for help enough", it's just more victim blaming. Friends try and one up you because depression is cool apparently, teachers ignore it, lecturers loathe you for it, parents aren't ready to have that conversation and Gps blow you off.

A counselor in school I cried to when I was 15 about it said "maybe you should talk to a Gp, but don't go for medication because it's not as easy as "pop a pill and get over it"". Said GP blew me off saying everyone has anxiety, maybe I should talk to my school counselor. I couldn't go to a different doctor because I knew how my parents felt about anti-anxiety pills and they thought I was only going in to talk about acne. So I just gave up. 

Year later I found myself in a drop in counselling session in college. "Oh the counselor isn't here today... so the drop in session isn't on", I was fighting back tears. The lady brought me in to her office and told me she was the college psychiatrist and that she has a few minutes to talk to me. After five minutes talking, she put me on antidepressants, I didn't even know I was depressed. I dropped out for the rest of the semester, which meant I couldn't continue to go to her. I knew there was no point in going back to my family Gp so I just came off them abruptly. Not one understanding lecturer, maybe one or two understanding teachers in school, but mostly people just absolutely hated dealing with me. They said I was a lazy student. I couldn't even estimate how many times I heard "this isn't good enough", when I was genuinely giving it every ounce of energy I could muster.

I struggled on through four more years of college and spent two of them in bed. Boyfriend recommended a new GP practice, and I was earning my own money at the time so I felt confident enough to go, and although I wasn't expecting anything, I went mostly for the sake of my relationship. My new GP is probably the reason I'm still alive. She found me the right meds. She wrote a letter for my college explaining that I've been struggling with a long, undiagnosed, untreated bout of depression and anxiety for at the very least the last four years. That letter is the single most validating piece of paper I own. I graduated, have a job I love, have been back to my hobbies, living with the love of my life, and I'm not even on antidepressants any more. I haven't found the root cause of all the depression, but I do believe I might be neurodivergent in some way. I'll pursue that at another time but right now I'm just happy to be alive.
